supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:44 UTC, ivy.chen's PowerShell process ran Compress-Archive against \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients, targeting C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon recorded creation of that ZIP shortly afterward.

At 13:44:37 UTC, ivy.chen launched Edge to quickshare-drop.net. At 13:48 UTC, the proxy recorded a 51,000,000-byte client-to-server tunnel to that domain under ivy.chen, and Zeek recorded approximately 51 MB sent in the corresponding proxy connection.

The large transfer followed creation of an archive of the Clients share and a browser launch to an unapproved file-sharing destination. Together, the timing, volume, and destination strongly support deliberate data exfiltration.

At 14:11 UTC, ivy.chen launched KB5034441_update.exe from C:\Windows\Temp with /quiet. The available process events do not establish what the executable did, but its location and timing are additional suspicious activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy CONNECT and Zeek records provide tunnel byte counts, but not the encrypted application payload or the exact files transmitted (T049-00159, T049-00161).
The records show creation of c.zip and a later large transfer, but do not directly prove that c.zip was the uploaded content (T049-00130, T049-00132, T049-00159).
The provided evidence contains no hash, signature validation, or execution outcome that establishes whether KB5034441_update.exe is malicious (T049-00243, T049-00244, T049-00275, T049-00276).
claims_not_established: The exact contents of c.zip or whether the 51 MB transfer included that archive.
Whether ivy.chen was acting knowingly, or whether the account or workstation was compromised.
The ownership or reputation of quickshare-drop.net beyond the provided inventory identifying no approved file-sharing service.
Whether KB5034441_update.exe executed malicious behavior or was related to the outbound transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and inspect c.zip and relevant source files; record hashes, contents, timestamps, and access history for the Clients share.
Obtain endpoint/browser download and upload artifacts, browser history, and any available proxy TLS inspection or destination-side transfer metadata to identify what was sent.
Analyze KB5034441_update.exe, including its hash, signature, provenance, and behavior; review endpoint telemetry for persistence, child processes, and subsequent network activity.
Interview ivy.chen and verify whether the archive creation and quickshare-drop.net transfer were authorized.
